Hi Elena / Marissa — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below (high level) and attached: Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx and subprocessors_list_20260511.csv.

1) Controller / Processor: Confirmed — Acme will be Controller; Redwood Inference will be Processor. Redwood will process data only per Acme's documented instructions and the DPA. We'll include language in the redline to make this explicit.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessors list. Process: we notify customers on material subprocessor changes. We can commit to a 30-day notice period for subprocessors that will handle PII, and provide the right to object; if Acme objects, we'll engage to provide alternative controls or onboarding options.

3) Breach notice SLA: Our standard is 72 hours for incidents materially impacting customer data. We recognize Acme prefers 48 hours; 48h is more disruptive operationally because it requires an accelerated triage/forensics window. We're willing to accept a 48-hour initial notification as a contractual commitment for material incidents on a case-by-case basis pending approval from our ops and security leadership. If Acme needs 48h as a hard requirement, please flag for us and we'll escalate, but note this may require a Dedicated deployment or higher SLA tier.

4) Data residency: For EU-only residency, we can commit to region-restricted hosting on our Dedicated or Private deployment options (and include contractual guarantees). For our hosted service we can offer regionally-restricted processing/at-rest storage for customer-owned data upon request (and document this in the DPA). We'll include explicit language about where logs are stored and retention windows.

5) PII retention & deletion: We can support a configurable retention window; 90 days is feasible. For deletion requests, subprocessors who store PII will be contractually obligated to delete or certify destruction within 30 days; we'll add that to the redline.

6) Logging & access controls: We provide audit logs (retention configurable), token-level usage breakdowns (no raw PII in logs unless explicitly sent), role-based access controls, and support for customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. We'll add these controls to the Security FAQ and redline.

7) SCCs / Export controls: We'll include standard contractual clauses where required and work with Acme on any additional export control obligations.

Attachments in this thread: Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx (contains proposed language for 48h / 72h options and subprocessors), subprocessors_list_20260511.csv, Security_FAQ.xlsx (already shared).

If helpful, Dev can confirm whether any hosted-product limitation prevents us from strictly guaranteeing EU-only logs for the hosted tier; Dev: can you confirm nuances re: log replication and Dedicated vs Hosted?


